stadt-bergpark-erschliessung-2010.title: Gesamterschließungskonzept Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe
stadt-bergpark-erschliessung-2010.publisher: Stadt Kassel — Stadtplanung, Bauaufsicht und Denkmalschutz
stadt-bergpark-erschliessung-2010.notes: Official 2010 access concept with a numbered 1–34 park inventory: Herkulesstatue, Grottenhof, Bassin mit Riesenkopf, Große Kaskade, Bassin mit Wasserfall, Felseneck, Steinhöfer-Wasserfall, Fontänenreservoir, Plutogrotte, Teufelsbrücke, Asch, Eremitage des Sokrates, Merkur-Tempel, Löwenburg, Sibyllengrotte, Pyramide, Vergils Grabmal, Aquädukt, Neuer Wasserfall, Jussow-Tempel, Fontänenteich, Musikpavillon, Flora, Halle des Sokrates, Pagode, Mulang, Roseninsel, Schloss, Weißensteinflügel, Gewächshaus, Marstall, Schlosshotel, Ballhaus and Schlossteich. Phase-2 maps component names to canonical nodes rather than inventing duplicate coordinates.

unesco-decision-37com8b33.title: Decision 37 COM 8B.33 — Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe
unesco-decision-37com8b33.notes: Authoritative inscription decision. It states that all water features except the New Waterfall remain operable, so New Waterfall is preserved as surviving but non-functional rather than treated as an active Wasserspiele station.

stadt-lac.title: Wasserspiele Station 7 — Lac
stadt-lac.notes: Primary current nomenclature source: water flows from the Fontänenteich to the Schlossteich called the Lac; the Lac was formed from a small fish pond in 1785–1791 under Heinrich Christoph Jussow.

hkh-orangerie-karlsaue.title: Orangerie
hkh-orangerie-karlsaue.notes: Official HKK location page explicitly places the Orangerie Palace in the Karlsaue. It is therefore not promoted as a Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe landmark; the relevant Bergpark plant building is the Großes Gewächshaus.
